resources.string: Please enter valid Package ID and Adgeist App ID

adIsResponsive = false, setAdDimension(AdSize(360, 360)).\n\nThe AdView measures itself from AdSize alone. If the server returns a creative of a different size, the SDK adopts the creative\'s size, re-measures this box, and reports the mismatch with an AW7 warning event.
Ad B - invalid ad unit, reserveSpace = false
This ad unit does not exist, so the load fails. Because reserveSpace is false, the AdView removes itself from the layout after the failed-load event (AW6) - the red box below should disappear.
Ad C - invalid ad unit, reserveSpace = true

Same invalid ad unit as Ad B, so it fails the same way. Because reserveSpace is true the AdView stays in the layout and keeps its 360dp x 360dp box - the blue box below should remain, empty, with nothing below it shifting up.

adIsResponsive = true, no AdSize set.

The container below is a fixed 300dp x 250dp box, so the AdView receives MeasureSpec.EXACTLY on both axes and takes both from the view tree. No warning is expected.

This is the only configuration that worked before per-axis measurement was added.

adIsResponsive = true, setAdDimension(AdSize.width(120)).

The ad sits in the right-hand column, which is wrap_content wide and match_parent tall. So:

height - MeasureSpec.EXACTLY, taken from the view tree
width - MeasureSpec.AT_MOST, taken from AdSize.width(120)

Before per-axis measurement the AT_MOST width was read as 'exactly this much' and the column swallowed the whole screen width.

adIsResponsive = true, setAdDimension(AdSize.height(50)).

The ad is the bottom row, which is match_parent wide and wrap_content tall. So:

width - MeasureSpec.EXACTLY, taken from the view tree
height - MeasureSpec.AT_MOST, taken from AdSize.height(50)

Before per-axis measurement the AT_MOST height was read as 'exactly this much' and this banner expanded to fill every remaining pixel of the screen.

A ScrollView measures its child\'s height with MeasureSpec.UNSPECIFIED, whose size is 0. A wrap_content row inside it inherits that, so the AdView is told nothing at all about its height.\n\nThis is the silent failure: the ad fetches and renders fine, but measures 0 tall and is never visible.
Ad B - no AdSize, measures 0 and warns
Nothing can determine this ad\'s height: the parent supplies no fixed height and no AdSize supplies one. The red box below stays empty and an AW4 warning event fires.
